A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ExpertAF and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G. Their matching content and complete PDF pages support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original model evaluations, ablations, and human ratings for commentary generation, demonstration retrieval, and pose generation.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds an evaluation of retrieval when suitable expert demonstrations are missing.

M1.justification: The architecture, objectives, and inference equations match. However, Section 3.4 replaces explicit frozen-LLM, mapper-only training for Ft and Fr with unspecified finetuning. Whether the trainable components changed, rather than their description alone, remains unclear.

E1.justification: The Ego-Exo4D basketball, soccer, and rock-climbing coverage remains. Appendix D adds a test scenario simulating unavailable correct expert demonstrations in the retrieval pool, extending evaluation conditions without adding a dataset or physical task.

E2.justification: Appendix D and Table 2 newly compare generated poses against poses extracted using ExpertAF's own retrieval branch, labeled 'ret. w/o GT'. This comparator was absent from the earlier pose-error comparison. Table 1's external baselines remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.4 changes the reported Ft/Fr training schedule from 10 epochs at 2e-2 to 5 epochs at 5e-5. Appendix D introduces exclusion of the 50 closest retrieval candidates and evaluation of the retrieved poses. Existing splits and principal metrics remain; rerunning the retained experiments is not established.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a robustness comparison testing whether pose generation helps when correct retrieval demonstrations are unavailable. Existing modality, alignment, global-pose, LLM-choice, and joint-training ablations, along with qualitative failure cases, are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4 newly reports paired t-tests with p < 0.05 for commentary-generation gains. v2 provides no corresponding statistical test. This adds significance reporting without establishing additional training runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds a 160 mm PA-MPJPE result for 'ret. w/o GT', and Appendix B.5 newly reports that 5.5% of samples were discarded during verification. Table 1, human-rating bars, and pre-existing Table 2 scores remain unchanged; no across-version performance gain is established.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, inference equations (1)–(3), temporal-alignment formulation, and training losses are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: actionable multimodal coaching, a weakly supervised dataset, three feedback outputs, and superiority over evaluated baselines. Added evidence does not redefine these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 newly interprets the 5.5% rejection rate as evidence of automated pipeline quality. Generation's usefulness without correct retrieval examples was already stated in v2 Section 3.1. Existing limitations concerning noisy poses, commentary granularity, and non-visible feedback remain.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies same-activity learner/expert pairing, revises training hyperparameters, and removes the explicit frozen-LLM/mapper-only specification. The abstract also drops the public code/data release promise while retaining the project-page link; actual resource availability cannot be determined from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The same 87 cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Changed reference back-links reflect pagination, and the new acknowledgement cites an already referenced work.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording edits, introduces the AF abbreviation, expands the university affiliation, and adds an acknowledgement and short explanations. The main section hierarchy and Appendix A–G organization remain.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a row and separators, while Table 1's caption highlights the privileged-input variant. Figure 4 receives minor border and caption edits. Existing figures are retained, with limited surrounding text and appendix reflow.

improvement.justification: The new Appendix D experiment supplies targeted evidence for the previously asserted benefit of generation when suitable retrieval examples are unavailable. Together with significance reporting and the verification rejection rate, this modestly strengthens empirical support. These gains are tempered by less explicit trainable-parameter disclosure and removal of the release promise; unchanged main results do not establish improved model performance.
